clue.text: This would be wrongly seen as poor in watts, without energy

definitions.text: This would be wrongly seen as poor in watts, without energy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the rearranged letters sit outside the energy symbol
taken wrongly, the letters of the phrase are read in a mistaken order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sceptic's remark that something would wrongly be judged short of power if it lacked energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges POOR IN WATTS and 'without' (outside) wraps that round E. The whole clue is the definition too: a generating plant would hardly be thought poor in watts.
explanation.definitionFit: A generating plant supplying electricity to the grid is anything but short of wattage, which is the joke of the whole-clue definition.

clue.text: Easily influenced to stay in shot

indicators.note: the staying word goes inside the shot

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a shot
to last is to stay or endure

explanation.surface: Someone easily swayed persuaded to stay put in a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the insertion signal; 'shot' is a photograph, not a gunshot or a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic means mouldable, so of a mind, readily shaped by others.

clue.text: Reporter attending start of week-long strike

indicators.note: start of points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: hack is a disparaging word for a journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist covers the start of a strike lasting a week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' gives W, with HACK after it; 'attending' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To whack is to strike hard, and a whack is a heavy blow.

clue.text: Arcane religious practice involving supporter, not leader

indicators.note: the rite takes the shortened supporter inside it

parts.note: a rite is a religious ceremony

indicators.note: the supporter word loses its first letter

parts.note: a second backs up a duellist or boxer

explanation.surface: An obscure religious ceremony includes a supporter who is not in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not leader' beheads the supporter, a duelling second, and 'involving' puts what is left inside the rite.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite means obscure and little known, a close synonym of arcane.

clue.text: Go over suggestion to involve Republican

indicators.note: the tip takes the Republican letter into it

parts.note: a tip is a helpful suggestion

explanation.surface: Reviewing a suggestion that involves a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to involve' puts R inside TIP. 'Go over' means fall, not review.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to stumble and fall over, which is to go over.

clue.text: Afraid, when climbing, to pass over most of fire

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to omit is to pass over

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: to fire someone up is to rouse them

explanation.surface: A nervous climber is told to skip most of a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when climbing' turns OMIT to TIMO; 'most of' trims ROUSE to ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Timorous means timid and fearful, a synonym for afraid.

clue.text: The Telegraph, say — not alluring in part of Wales

indicators.note: not says the alluring word is taken away

parts.note: Glamorgan is a historic county of south Wales
glam, short for glamorous, means alluring

explanation.surface: The Telegraph newspaper judged unglamorous somewhere in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: GLAMORGAN is a county in south Wales; 'not' removes GLAM from it.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a newspaper or journal speaking for a group; the Telegraph is one example.

clue.text: Recent British monarchs touring university in high style

indicators.note: the monarchs go round the university letter

parts.note: GR and ER, George Rex and Elizabeth Regina, recent British monarchs

explanation.surface: Recent royals visiting a university in grand fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The monarchs give GR AND ER; 'touring' puts U inside ER, so GR AND E(U)R.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is splendour and magnificence, living in a grand, elevated manner.

clue.text: Fix Maine? Little money there to secure it

indicators.note: the coin holds the state letters fast inside

parts.note: the cent is the small coin used in the USA, where Maine is
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: Repairing Maine on the cheap, with small change to hold it together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' signals insertion; 'there' ties the little money to Maine's own country, so a US coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To cement is to bind firmly, so to fix in place.

clue.text: An old word, failing to capture a disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: failing to take in, so the following letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: an archaism is an old-fashioned word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone using an old word misses the chance to describe a disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to capture' means leaving out the clue's 'a'; the archaism loses one of its two As.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism is the political creed of no government, and anarchy is lawless disorder, a loose but fair link.

clue.text: Try anything, initially, to escape storm in valley

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: letting a letter escape means removing it from the word

parts.note: to storm is to rage

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Advice to try anything to get out of a storm while caught in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' picks the first letter of 'anything', and 'to escape' removes that letter from the word for storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorge is a steep narrow ravine, a kind of valley cut between rock walls.

clue.text: Attractive Royal appearing after cheers

indicators.note: the royal is placed after the thanks in the answer

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers
a king is a royal

explanation.surface: A handsome royal makes an entrance just after the applause.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you, as is 'cheers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking in its dated sense means charming or appealing, as in a taking smile.

clue.text: Soldiers caper, stealing knight's weapons

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: the soldiers and the caper take the knight into their midst

parts.note: to caper is to dance about
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Mischievous soldiers make off with a knight's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stealing' signals insertion: the soldiers and the caper together swallow the chess knight, N not K.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is military supplies, especially artillery and munitions, so weapons collectively.

clue.text: Farm animal that is eating river shellfish

indicators.note: the cow and IE swallow the river letter

parts.note: a cow is a farm animal
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A cow grazing by a river ends up eating a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' signals insertion into the animal plus the abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowrie is a sea snail with a glossy shell once used as money: loosely a shellfish.

clue.text: Audible comment about pointlessness of selling things in blizzard conditions

indicators.note: audible tells us the answer sounds like a spoken remark

parts.words: comment about pointlessness of selling things
parts.note: a doubter asking why tout, that is why bother selling

explanation.surface: A street seller doubts there is any point in trading during a snowstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audible' signals the spoken 'Why tout?', to tout being to peddle wares.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiteout is weather where snow and cloud blot out all visibility and contrast.

clue.text: Make a bet about regulation regarding discharge

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective answer

indicators.note: the bet goes around the regulation

parts.note: to punt is British slang for to gamble
a rule is a regulation

explanation.surface: A gambler wagers on what the rules say about being discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the bet goes round the regulation; punting is British slang for gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Purulent means consisting of or producing pus, the discharge from an infected wound.

clue.text: Theatre ultimately invested in opening, not ending

indicators.note: the theatre's last letter is placed inside the opening word

parts.note: uncasing something is opening it up

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A theatre whose run finally got funding at its opening, with no closing night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E from 'Theatre', which 'invested in' puts inside UNCASING.
explanation.definitionFit: Unceasing means continuing without stop, never coming to an end.

clue.text: Consumer wanting their own point accepted by channel

indicators.note: taken in by the channel, so it goes inside

parts.note: a canal is a channel of water
a nib is the point of a pen

explanation.surface: A shopper wanting their point heard on a television channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' signals insertion. 'Consumer' means one who eats, and the channel is a waterway, not television.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannibal eats others of its kind, so it is an eater with a taste for its own species.

clue.text: Moral type keeping a detective back — what's the cost?

indicators.note: the prig holds the reversed pair within

parts.note: a prig is a self-righteously moral person

indicators.note: back says the next pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious person employs a private eye, and wonders what it costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the 'a' and the short word for detective; 'keeping' puts the result inside the moral type.
explanation.definitionFit: A price tag is the label stating cost, so it answers the question of how much something is.

clue.text: Father with speed identifying Father's position

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
pacy means quick, having speed

explanation.surface: A dad in a hurry discovers what the Holy Father's office involves.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'Father' is the Pope: the definition is his office.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the office of the Pope, the Holy Father of the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Flier, not fully fit, seen returning around part of airship

indicators.note: the reversed letters go around the airship part
returning means that shortened word is read backwards
the word for fit loses its last letter, so it is incomplete

parts.note: to suit is to fit or match
the car is the passenger compartment slung under an airship

explanation.surface: An unfit aviator is spotted coming back near an airship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fully' trims the fit word, 'seen returning' reverses it, and 'around' wraps it round the airship's passenger car.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew on wings of wax and feathers, the archetypal flier.

clue.text: Nothing missing from diva's performance, say, in spa rooms

indicators.note: the zero-like letter is absent from the performance phrase

parts.note: a diva might sing a solo aria
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A diva's singing at a spa has a note missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing from' removes one O from SOLO ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Solaria are sunrooms or sunbed rooms, plural of solarium, found at spas.

clue.text: Long to suppress most of restraint? That'll be nice

indicators.note: the longing holds down the restraint inside it

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it

indicators.note: only most of the restraint is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: a leash restrains a dog

explanation.surface: Longing to rein in a restraint would be a nice outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the restraint's last letter, and 'to suppress' puts the rest inside the word for long.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant and nice are everyday synonyms for agreeable.

clue.text: Say nothing over one ignoring a hot dish from the East

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the hush word sits above
the hot letter is left out of the hushing word

parts.note: shush is a call to keep quiet
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about someone who won't touch spicy Eastern food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops one H from SHUSH to give SUSH; 'from the East' is the definition, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, Japan being in the Far East.

clue.text: Composer giving us a lot of hell?

indicators.note: read the answer as two pieces given us with a joining word between them, so that word sits inside the trimmed word
a lot of, but not all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as the word itself, the place of torment
the question mark tells the solver to read the answer playfully, with the joining word 'and' sitting between its outer pieces

explanation.surface: A composer whose music puts listeners through torment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving us' and the question mark ask for a self-referential split, 1,3,2: the outer pieces joined give most of hell ('a lot of' drops one L).
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was the German-born British composer of Messiah and the Water Music.

clue.text: Second person in Paris coming in to block piece of information

indicators.note: the French word goes into the blocking word

parts.note: to dam is to block
tu is French for you, the second person

explanation.surface: A French 'you' arrives to stop a fact getting through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in to' signals insertion; the French familiar 'you' goes into the word for block.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single fact or item of data.

clue.text: Crossword? Hard work not new

indicators.note: not says the abbreviation for new is removed

parts.note: a grind is tedious hard work

explanation.surface: A crossword that's hard work but nothing novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes N from GRIND. The question mark shows 'Crossword' defines by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is the pattern of squares a crossword is built on, so it stands for the puzzle itself.

clue.text: Suit line adopted by boys in uniform

indicators.note: taken in by the boys, so it goes inside

parts.note: Cubs are junior Scouts who wear uniform

explanation.surface: Uniformed boys take on a line of clothing that suits them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' puts L inside CUBS; 'Suit' is a card suit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Stone used in wall, say, in brief

indicators.note: the stone letters are put inside the barrier

parts.note: a wall is an example of a barrier
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: A builder describes stone used in a wall, briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' signals insertion; 'brief' is a noun, British slang for a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is slang for a barrister, the lawyer who takes the brief to argue a case in court.

clue.text: Shakespeare character, explorer carrying black instrument

parts.note: Viola is the heroine of Twelfth Night

indicators.note: the explorer holds the black letter inside

parts.note: Vasco da Gama was the Portuguese navigator who reached India by sea
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean heroine joins an explorer who carries something black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts B inside DA GAMA, giving DA GAMBA after VIOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The viola da gamba is a bowed string instrument of the viol family, held between the legs.
